title: Minimum Viable Cycle Plan and Rolling Surge Strategy
creator: Monica Reyes
description:
Goal: Provide a lightweight, repeatable cycle planning template that lets PMs commit to a defensible minimum viable cycle plan (MVCP) and an explicit rolling surge strategy for staffing and scope cuts. The MVCP balances committed OKR work with a protected runway for unplanned incidents and cross-team dependencies. The rolling surge strategy defines pre-approved triggers, role-level surge commitments, and a substitution matrix to enable fast, low-friction rebalancing without leadership bottlenecks.

Scope: this ticket produces the MVCP template, an annotated decision grid for scope cuts, a staffing matrix by role (PM/Eng/Design/SRE/Support), examples of pre-approved deferrable work, and communication templates for cycle mid-point re-triage. It also includes a small automation checklist for cycle kickoff and surge activation (Slack templates + short form DSAT).

Trade-offs and constraints:
- We keep the MVCP intentionally minimal so small teams can complete planning in 1–2 hours; full capacity models remain in parallel but optional.
- Surge commitments prioritize critical path roles; excessive pre-commits reduce flexibility for high-volatility cycles.
- The decision grid favors user-facing OKRs and SLA/Reliability work over internal tooling when utilization is ambiguous.

Key artifacts to produce:
- MVCP template (Google Doc) with: top-line commitments, guardrail thresholds, buffer allocation, and a 1-page justification for each committed OKR.
- Scope Decision Grid (confluence) with prioritized cut levels (A: keep, B: deferable, C: target for cut) and cut triggers.
- Staffing Matrix spreadsheet with estimated FTE allocation per week and role-level surge multipliers.
- Slack/Email templates for surge activation and mid-cycle status updates.

Acceptance Criteria:
- MVCP template is adopted by at least 3 product pods in the next cycle pilot.
- Decision Grid includes three real examples from prior cycles and a rule-of-thumb scoring rubric.
- Staffing matrix yields a sample plan that stays within 90% of committed weekly capacity for pilot pods.

Success metrics:
- Pilot adoption: 3 pods adopt MVCP within two cycles.
- Reduction in mid-cycle scope churn: 30% fewer last-minute scope cuts compared to baseline.
- Time-to-decision on surge activation: median <= 24 hours across pilot pods.

Links and references:
- Planning checklist template: https://drive.redwood/planning/mvcp-template (draft)
- Example decision grid: https://confluence.redwood/wikis/decision-grid-examples
- Capacity model spreadsheet: https://sheets.redwood/capacity/matrix-2026-w10
- Related OKR playbook: https://confluence.redwood/wikis/okrs/playbook-2025
